dorsal_wing_plumage_topography.wing_bar_presence_and_contrast: Individual coverts exhibit high-contrast, thick pale-grey fringes against dark charcoal centers; while not forming distinct solid horizontal bars, the cumulative effect creates a high-contrast repetitive band-like texture.
dorsal_wing_plumage_topography.flight_feather_edge_geometry: Sharp, prominent pale-grey linear boundaries are clearly visible along the trailing edges of the folded primary and secondary feathers.

crown_and_nape_macro_patterns.crown_to_mantle_demarcation: A visible but gradational transition where the fine, streaked texture of the nape abruptly gives way to the larger, coarsely scalloped pattern of the mantle.

other_distinctive_markers: Pronounced repetitive scalloping effect across the entire dorsal surface caused by extreme contrast between feather centers and wide margins.
